General information.Name: Environmental Impacts Associated with Intensive Production in Pig Farms in Mexico through Life Cycle Assessment
General information.Category: A:Agriculture, forestry and fishing/014:Animal production/0146:Raising of swine/pigs
General information.Description: In this research, environmental impacts associated with the intensive production of pigs on a farm in Mexico were determined through the application of life cycle assessment methodology. The research was focused on the following stages of the product system: (i) pig rearing and growth phases; (ii) production operations in the pig-house; (iii) the supply of feed. The life cycle inventory database was mainly made up of data collected in field visits to local farms. The functional unit was defined as one finished swine weighing 124 kg. The results for the selected impact categories of carbon, water, and energy footprints were 538.62 kg CO2eq, 21.34 m³, and 1773.79 MJ, respectively. The greatest impact was generated in the final stages of pig fattening, mainly due to the large quantity of feed supplied. The impacts caused by operation of the pig farm were less significant, their contribution in all cases was less than a third of the total quantified values. The energy conversion of pig slurry improves the environmental performance of the product system by reducing the carbon footprint.
General information.Tags: pig production, life cycle assessment, carbon, water and energy footprint, environmental impacts
General information.Technology Description: The methodology was based on ISO 14040: 2006 and ISO 14044: 2006. To quantify environmental impacts from GHG emissions, ReCiPe methodology (v. 1.01) was used, based on ISO 14067: 2018. The method of vulnerability assessment and water accounting (WAVE) was used to quantify the water footprint, in accordance with ISO 14046: 2014. The energy footprint was based on the accumulated energy demand (CED) methodology.

processDocumentation.LCI method: The methodology used for this work was based on ISO 14040: 2006 and ISO 14044: 2006.
processDocumentation.Process type: Cradle-to-gate life cycle analysis of intensive pig production, from feed production and input transport to a finished pig ready for sale.
processDocumentation.Modeling constants: Capital goods, such as the construction of facilities, were excluded. For enteric gases, the Tier-1 method was used with methane emission factors from literature. A factor of 16.6% of losses from the distribution in the electrical grid was included.
processDocumentation.Data source information: Primary data was collected through field interviews and questionnaires with personnel at pig farms. Secondary data for food supplies were obtained from Ecoinvent database (v. 3.7.1). Other secondary data were compiled from local and international references and technical reports from the national energy sector.
processDocumentation.Data selection: Capital goods like facility construction were excluded as their contributions were not considered significant. The study focuses on pig rearing and growth, production operations in the pig-house, and feed supply.
processDocumentation.Data treatment: Material and energy balances were carried out to determine all flows. Mass allocation was applied for co-products. Energy flows were quantified using energy conversion, efficiency, and loss factors.
processDocumentation.Sampling procedure: Field work consisted of: (i) verification of the stages of the pig's productive cycle; (ii) knowledge of daily activities in the pig house; (iii) identification of supplies (feed, water, energy); (iv) feeding in different rearing stages; (v) management of waste generated. Questionnaires were prepared for application to operational agents.
